title: Confidence-Gated Parallel Decoding with a Length-Aware Step Budget
one_liner: Decide how many parallel refinement passes a sequence gets from its own length and per-position confidence, instead of fixing the step count in advance.
description: A non-autoregressive decoder that spends a variable number of refinement passes per sequence. Each pass predicts every masked position in parallel; a position is frozen once its confidence crosses a threshold, and the pass count is allocated from the predicted output length rather than fixed as a constant K. The claim is that the reported speedups of fixed-K non-autoregressive decoding vanish on long outputs precisely because K does not scale with length, and that making the budget length-aware recovers them.

sections.technique: Masked-denoising decoder. Per pass: predict logits for every unfrozen position in parallel, freeze positions whose max-probability exceeds tau, re-mask the rest. The pass budget is B(T) = a + b*log(T) with a, b learned on a held-out split; tau is a fixed hyperparameter in the first version.
open_questions: Does the number of passes needed actually grow with output length, or is it the number of *hard* positions that grows?
Should the budget be predicted per sequence before decoding, or allocated greedily while decoding?
Is a fixed confidence threshold enough, or does tau have to be calibrated per position?
sections.open_risks: If the hard positions are clustered (rare vocabulary, named entities), a length-based budget spends passes in the wrong place and the speedup does not materialize.

nodes.text: Generate ideas from gap_0c5b557e (sequential decoding) and gap_1fda3e27 (speedups vanish on long outputs).

nodes.title: Larger denoiser, same fixed schedule
nodes.text: Keep the fixed-K mask-predict decoder and spend the budget on a wider denoiser, so each pass resolves more positions.

nodes.title: Confidence-Gated Parallel Decoding with a Length-Aware Step Budget
nodes.text: The field fixes K because the original papers did. Relax that: let the pass budget depend on output length and freeze positions by confidence.

nodes.title: Anytime decoding as an interruptible solver
nodes.text: Treat decoding as an anytime algorithm from the planning literature: any interruption must return a complete, valid output whose quality rises monotonically with time spent.

nodes.title: Fuse mask-predict with a diffusion schedule
nodes.text: Combine mask-predict refinement with a learned discrete-diffusion corruption schedule so the masking rate is trained rather than hand-set.
